finding.text: A post-commit hook system already exists and the diff builds a second one (law 6): `Server/git-hooks/post-commit.mjs` is installed as `.git/hooks/post-commit` (marker `servex-task-commits`) and logs `{"commit":"<12 hash>"}` to the task log that `SERVEX_TASK` names (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:1505`), with its own readme `Server/git-hooks/readme.md` and test. The work should extend that one module (add the session lookup, the trailer and the files list there), not add `.githooks/` + `Server/CommitLog.mjs` next to it. The brief's line "No core.hooksPath is set today" is true, but it hid the fact that hooks are already installed.

The merge-time step this task reports (`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, `Server/doc/commit-log.md:13`) would silently turn off both hooks installed in `.git/hooks/` today. `core.hooksPath` replaces that folder, so the current post-commit logger stops, and so does `post-merge`, which runs `Server/clarity.mjs look ai2` after merges that touch ai2. The new `.githooks/` has no post-merge. Neither the doc nor the report mentions this.

Indexing is now stale. `Server/readme.md:60` still calls `git-hooks/` "the git hooks every worktree shares", and the new line under it indexes a second hooks system. `Server/git-hooks/readme.md` was not touched. Once fix 1 folds the work into `Server/git-hooks/`, update that readme and `Server/doc/commit-log.md` (or move the doc into the module), and drop the duplicate readme line.

The failure line uses a new shape, `{"failure":{at,module,why}}` (`Server/CommitLog.mjs:46`), while the other `failures.jsonl` writers use `{at, fail:{kind,…}}` (`public/framework/ext/ErrorLog/ErrorLog.js:44`, `Servex/WorktreeWatch.js:269`). Anyone who `follow`s `ai/sessions` would get a line that no other failure reader parses. Use `fail:{kind:"commit",…}`.

Commits made by the Servex process itself (the LogSweeper batches in `Servex/LogSweeper.js:107`, and `merge.mjs` when Servex runs it) carry no `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`. Each of those commits will write a failure line, so the log fills with expected noise. Either skip commits whose author is a known machine writer, or say in the doc that these lines are expected. There is no loop: `**/failures.jsonl` is git-ignored (`.gitignore:232`).

The brief asked the builder to check that `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is really set. The task log (`session.jsonl`) holds only the "ready" line: no log or decision line records that check, nor the versioned-hooks choice that `brief-common.md` requires. I checked it for a Servex agent: the same uuid is set in both Bash and PowerShell. A VS Code tab is still unverified.

The two systems disagree on the commit line's shape: a string `commit` here, and the old hook's 12-character string. `public/framework/ai/AISession/SessionTimelineRows.js:84` reads `l.commit?.hash` and `l.commit?.what`, so either shape renders as an empty "Commit :" row. Pick one shape when you merge the hooks and make that reader match it.

What works: `node Server/CommitLog.test.mjs` passes ("PASS … (6 checks)", run in `worktrees/truth-commits` at 2ca329517). It covers the commit line with its hash and files, the trailer, and, with no session, no line plus one failure line while the commit still succeeds. Session lookup, the never-block exit and the write through `RecordWriter.write` are sound, and the `SessionRecord.log_file` path matches `SpawnLog.file_of`.
